content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "For each firm, compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using annual financials lagged at least 4 months. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "When inventory builds faster than sales, it signals demand overestimation and future writedowns or margin pressure, which the market is slow to price.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)"}, {"name": "Order Backlog to Assets", "construction": "Divide reported order backlog (Compustat item OB) by total assets (item AT), using annual data lagged 4 months. Form cross-sectional deciles.", "rationale": "Order backlog is a forward-looking demand indicator that is disclosed but underweighted by investors relative to reported earnings.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Selling Expense Efficiency Change", "construction": "Compute the change in the ratio of SG&A expense (item XSGA) to sales (item SALE) from the prior fiscal year to the current one; measure = -(current ratio minus prior ratio). Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Improving operating efficiency (falling overhead per dollar of sales) signals management execution not yet reflected in valuation multiples.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (improving efficiency)"}, {"name": "Deferred Tax Signal", "construction": "Compute the change in the net deferred tax liability (from Compustat deferred taxes item TXDB) scaled by lagged total assets, annual data lagged 4 months. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Large increases in deferred tax liabilities often reflect aggressive book-vs-tax accounting that inflates reported earnings and reverses later.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Acceleration", "construction": "For each firm compute capex (item CAPX) scaled by lagged property plant and equipment (item PPENT) minus the firm's own 3-year average of that ratio. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Spikes in investment relative to a firm's normal pace tend to be followed by disappointing returns as overinvestment erodes future free cash flow.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Dividend Initiation Persistence Momentum", "construction": "Flag firms that paid a dividend (item DVC > 0) in each of the trailing 3 years with strictly non-decreasing dividends per share, and rank remaining firms by the compound growth rate of dividends per share over that window.", "rationale": "Consistently rising dividends credibly signal sustainable cash flows and managerial confidence that the market underappreciates.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (steadily rising dividends)"}, {"name": "Gross Margin Stability", "construction": "Compute the standard deviation of quarterly gross margin (GP = SALE minus COGS, divided by SALE, using Compustat quarterly items SALEQ and COGSQ) over the trailing 12 quarters; measure = -stddev. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Stable gross margins indicate durable competitive advantage and lower cash-flow risk that is only partially compensated by the market.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (more stable margins)"}, {"name": "Turnover-Adjusted Momentum", "construction": "Take standard 12-month minus 1-month past return, and within each momentum decile sort further by average monthly share turnover (CRSP volume divided by shares outstanding) over the same 12 months; measure = momentum residualized on turnover, favoring low-turnover winners.", "rationale": "Momentum on low-attention (low-turnover) stocks reflects slower information diffusion and continues longer than high-turnover momentum.", "higher_returns_for": "high past return combined with low turnover"}, {"name": "Cash Productivity", "construction": "Compute operating cash flow proxy (item IB plus item DP, income before extraordinary items plus depreciation) divided by market value of equity (CRSP price times shares), annual data lagged 4 months. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Cash-based profitability relative to price is harder to manipulate than accrual earnings yield and captures genuine value the market discounts.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Analyst Coverage Deficit", "construction": "Regress number of covering analysts (IBES) on log market cap and log book-to-market cross-sectionally each month; measure = negative of the residual (firms with fewer analysts than their size/value peers predict).", "rationale": "Stocks with abnormally low coverage relative to observable characteristics are underfollowed, carry higher information risk, and earn a premium as coverage catches up.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (coverage deficit)"}]}
